claim: AutoProbe dynamically selects layers and token positions via attention for probing code correctness (compilability, functionality, security) and beats a fixed last-token-last-layer probe (Openia).
stance_target: probe beats fixed-layer probe on code correctness
quoted_support: AutoProbe consistently outperforms the baselines. For security assessment, AUTOPROBE surpasses the state-of-the-art white-box approach by 18%.

breadth.confidence_families: white-box hidden-state probe (AutoProbe attention-weighted layer/token selection), Openia last-token-last-layer probe, black-box CodeBERT/CodeT5+ classifiers, in-house and external (o4-mini) LLM-as-judge (Sec 4.3)
breadth.model_families_and_sizes: DeepSeek Coder 1.3B/6.7B, Code Llama 7B/13B, CodeGemma 7B, Magicoder 7B (Sec 4.2, Table 3)
breadth.reasoning_models: not present as studied subjects; o4-mini used only as external judge (Sec 4.3)
breadth.elicitation_formats: zero-shot judge prompts (in-house and external); no numeric verbal confidence elicitation
breadth.benchmarks: HumanEval, MBPP, DevEval, SecurityEval, CWEval, CodeGuard+, SALLM (Sec 4.1)
breadth.label_source: compilation, test execution, Bandit/CodeQL static analysis for security (Sec 4.1)
breadth.label_independence: labels from execution/static analysis independent of probes
breadth.calibration_metrics: accuracy, precision, recall, F1 only; no ECE/Brier (searched: calibrat)
breadth.causal_intervention: ablation of selector module only (RQ2); no causal intervention on hidden states
